skill_traces.query:
Tim: Hey John! Haven't talked to you in a bit but wanted to let you know I read this awesome book about castles in the UK. It was so interesting and blew me away! I dream of visiting them one day.
John: Hey Tim! Great to hear from you. Learning about different cultures and seeing historical architecture fascinates me. Visiting castles is really on my bucket list. Just look at this one; what a sight! I'm so excited to explore the world and experience these gorgeous places. On that note, how's your fantasy writing going?
Tim: That castle looks amazing! I hope I get to visit it someday. My writing is going well: I'm in the middle of fantasy novel and it's a bit nerve-wracking but so exciting! All my hard work is paying off. Writing brings such joy and it's incredible how it can create a whole new world. Thanks so much for believing in me!
John: That's great! I'm glad your writing is going well. It must be exciting to see it all come together. Keep going! Do you have a specific source of inspiration for your stories?
Tim: Thanks! Books, movies, and real-life experiences all fire up my creativity. For example, reading about castles in the UK gave me loads of ideas. Plus, certain authors are like goldmines of inspiration for me. Connecting with the things I love makes writing even more fun.
John: Wow! Sounds like a great mix. Is there a particular author whose work inspires you?
Tim: J.K. Rowling is such an inspiring writer. Her books are so captivating with their detail and creative storytelling. She can definitely transport readers into another world and make them feel so much. I'm always taking notes on her style for my own writing.
John: Cool! How long have you been reading her works?
Tim: I've been reading her stuff for a long time. Her stories have been with me and still inspire me. There's something special about her writing that really speaks to me.
John: Wow, some authors really have such an influence on us! They become part of our life and affect our interests. Do you have a favorite J.K. Rowling quote?
Tim: Yeah! There's a quote by J.K. Rowling that I really like: "Turn on the light - happiness hides in the darkest of times." That's how I keep hope alive during tough times.
John: Nice quote! It reminds us to stay positive and find joy even in hard times. It's a guiding light when things get rough. I appreciate you sharing it!
Tim: Nice job, John! What did you write on that whiteboard?
John: On that whiteboard, I wrote down some motivational quotes and strategies to help me stay focused and push through tough workouts. It really helps me stay motivated and keep improving.
Tim: That's awesome! Visual reminders and strategies can really help in staying motivated. It's cool that you have those quotes to keep you going during tough workouts.
John: This plaque I keep on my desk is a constant reminder to believe in myself. It helps me trust my abilities and face any obstacles. Having physical reminders like this really helps me stay motivated.
Tim: That's awesome! What keeps you motivated during challenging times?
John: My teammates believing in me and my love for improving my skills keep me going, even when things get tough. I don't want to let them down.
Tim: Nice one! What do you reckon makes them such a good support?
John: They always support me, even when I make mistakes. Their encouragement keeps me going.
Tim: That's key, having a strong support network can really help with what we're trying to do. Do you have people you can lean on outside of sports?
John: Yeah, I'm lucky - I have people who are super supportive, always there for me no matter what.
Tim: Awesome! Having people who lift us up is essential. I'm grateful I have friends and family who support me - it's huge.
John: Having loved ones who support us is so important. My family is always there for me.
Tim: Wow, look at this great group! Are these your people?
John: Yeah, definitely! That's my fam hanging out. Being with them brings me so much happiness and helps me remember what's important. My team is like my second family too.
Tim: That looks fun! What else do you do with them?
John: What people usually do when you hang out with friends and family - movies, dinner out. And what are your favorite activities for fun?
Tim: I love going on road trips with friends and family, exploring and hiking or playing board games. And in my free time, I enjoy curling up with a good book, escaping reality and getting lost in different worlds. That's what I'm talking about.
John: Yep, I totally get it! Cuddling up with a book is my chill time. And when I'm away from the court, cooking is therapy for me. It's a good way to be creative and experiment with flavors while taking a break. Here's a photo of me cooking a meal.
Tim: That slow cooker meal looks yum! Cooking is a great way to chill and be creative. Do you have any favorite recipes you can show me?
John: Definitely! I make this yummy honey garlic chicken with roasted veg a lot. It's one of my favorites. I'm always trying out new recipes, so let me know if you want suggestions!
Tim: Mmm, that sounds delicious, John! Can I get the recipe for it?
John: Sure thing! I can write it down for you and mail it to you.
Tim: Can't wait to try it. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
John: No worries. Hope you enjoy it! Let me know how it turns out.
Tim: Sure thing! Thanks. Great talking to you. Take care!
John: It was nice chatting with you. Talk to you later!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Objects as Reminders of Values
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a physical object that serves as a reminder, symbol, or inspiration for a personal value or goal.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes an object as a reminder or symbol of a value or goal, create a `state` candidate for the object and a `preference` candidate for the value/goal.
Use the speaker's exact wording and message evidence to link both candidates.
During CRUD, this rule requires no special handling; process candidates normally.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Start of Specific Creative Work
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user confirms starting or recently beginning a specific creative work.
content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.
